title: Rollout wait fails the idempotent deploy: no push means no digest to compare
description:
Found on the first re-deploy after z1b landed. z1b is working — it correctly refused a deploy whose rollout had not converged, which is exactly the false-success bug it was written to kill. But it fails the IDEMPOTENT path, which is the common case after the first deploy:

  Error: the factory deployed, but the ticks-orchestrator container rollout could not be confirmed:
  wranglers deploy output named no digest-pinned ticks-orchestrator image, so there is nothing to
  compare the application against

Cause, confirmed in the deploy log: when the image is unchanged wrangler prints "Image already exists remotely, skipping push" and emits NO digest line. z1b reads the digest out of wranglers output, finds none, and reports a failure. So a deploy that changes nothing — the safest deploy there is — reports a rollout it cannot confirm.

Fix: when no image was pushed, the image is by definition already the one the application should be serving. Resolve the expected digest another way rather than giving up: read it from the staged bundle or from the application record and compare, or treat "nothing pushed" as already-converged after verifying the application is not mid-transition. Do NOT weaken the case z1b exists for — a deploy that DID push and did not converge must still fail.

Second finding from the same session, worth folding in: the 5m poll bound expired roughly one poll before the rollout converged (the application reported state=provisioning with the new digest within ~30s of the timeout). The bound is close to reality rather than generous — consider raising it, and consider that state=provisioning with the CORRECT digest already means the new image is serving.

acceptance_criteria: A deploy that pushes nothing confirms the rollout instead of failing; a deploy that pushes and does not converge still fails nonzero naming the reason; the poll bound is justified against an observed rollout rather than guessed.
